MEMORANDUM
 ATO:           PCTPA Board of Directors                                       DATE: October 28, 2026

FROM:           Mike Costa, Principal Transportation Planner

 SUBJECT:       9:00 AM - PUBLIC HEARING: 2026 UNMET TRANSIT NEEDS
                ASSESSMENT AND PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT EFFORTS

ACTION REQUESTED
Conduct a public hearing to solicit and obtain public testimony on potential unmet transit needs
that may exist in Placer County.

BACKGROUND
Pursuant to the Transportation Development Act (TDA), the Unmet Transit Needs (UTN)
Assessment is one of PCTPA’s key annual administrative responsibilities as the Regional
Transportation Planning Agency (RTPA) for Placer County (excluding the Tahoe Basin). The
TDA provides two funding sources for public transit: Local Transportation Funds (LTF) and State
Transit Assistance (STA) funds. While STA funding is solely restricted to supporting public
transit service needs (e.g., operational expenses, capital fleet/equipment purchases, and other
administrative support), LTF can be used by Placer County’s incorporated cities/town and
unincorporated jurisdictions for other purposes, such as bicycle/pedestrian infrastructure and/or
street and road maintenance/repair, if it is determined that there are no unmet transit needs that are
reasonable to meet within the region encompassing those jurisdictions.

Each year, PCTPA conducts an extensive outreach process to solicit public comments regarding
potential unmet transit needs throughout the urban and rural areas of Placer County. While the
Tahoe Regional Planning Agency (TRPA) administers the UTN Assessment process for the
immediate Tahoe Basin, PCTPA works closely with TRPA to identify any potential transit need(s)
that may be located immediately outside of the Basin within the portions of Placer County that are
under PCTPA’s administrative authority (i.e., unincorporated areas between the Tahoe Basin and
City of Truckee, including the Donner Lake, Olympic Valley, Alpine Meadows and Northstar
resort areas). Comments received during this process are then evaluated by PCTPA staff,
PCTPA’s Transit Operators Working Group (TOWG) and the Social Services Transportation
Advisory Council (SSTAC), which collectively consist of the region’s transit operators, staff
representatives from each incorporated city/town within Placer County, including the County of
Placer, and other social service transportation providers, advocates, and public stakeholders.
Specific “unmet transit need” and “reasonable to meet” definitions and criteria that have been
adopted by PCTPA’s Board of Directors are used to make unmet transit needs findings (refer to
Attachment 1 for the current definitions and criteria, adopted in February 2022). Following the
evaluation of all public comments, PCTPA staff prepares a report with findings for the PCTPA
Board’s review and adoption. Should there be findings regarding unmet transit needs that are
reasonable to meet, the PCTPA Board must direct LTF revenues to those needs before local
jurisdictions can claim them for other purposes described previously, above.

DISCUSSION
For this year’s UTN Assessment process, PCTPA released an online public survey (available in
English, Spanish and Tagalog) on September 1st, which will be available through October 31st.
Additionally, per TDA requirements, at least one public hearing is being held to solicit comments
regarding potential unmet transit needs in Placer County, which will occur at the October 28th
PCTPA Board meeting held in Auburn. The public hearing has been noticed in the Auburn local
newspaper and advertised with the survey’s availability through informational materials that
PCTPA has released to local and regional media networks, each TOWG stakeholder, and through
its e-mail contact lists and social media platforms. Additionally, PCTPA staff submitted
informational materials to each local jurisdiction to help further promote the UTN Assessment
process and available survey during scheduled public meetings of their respective governing
bodies (i.e., Town/City Council or Board of Supervisor meeting) occurring in September and
October. Lastly, as part of other agency outreach efforts, UTN materials were provided at pop-
events PCTPA held in several of the Placer region’s local jurisdictions during September and early
October.

Public comments regarding potential unmet transit needs can be submitted during the October 28th
public hearing, via phone at (530) 823-4029, via e-mail at mcosta@pctpa.net, and through the on-
line survey available at Unmet_Transit_Needs_Survey. The public comment period for this year’s
UTN Assessment process will conclude on October 31, 2026. Following the closure of the public
comment period, PCTPA staff will summarize and evaluate the comments received with the
TOWG and SSTAC members and then prepare a report identifying findings regarding any unmet
transit needs that are reasonable to meet. That report with findings will formally be presented to
the PCTPA Board of Directors for adoption in February 2027.

MEMORANDUM
 TO:             WPCTSA Board of Directors                                         DATE: October 28, 2026

 FROM:           Mike Costa, Principal Transportation Planner

 SUBJECT:        SERVICE POLICY REVISIONS FOR THE PLACER RIDES PROGRAM

ACTION REQUESTED
Approve the revisions to the Placer Rides Program service policies, as provided.

BACKGROUND
In October 2025, the WPCTSA Board of Directors approved revisions to the Placer Rides
Program service policies that became effective on July 1, 2026, concurrent with the start of
WPCTSA’s new administrative agreement with MOVE Stanislaus Transportation, Inc. (MOVE).
A general review of the Placer Rides Program’s service policies and past mileage reimbursement
practices was conducted following MOVE’s assumption of all administrative responsibilities
from the prior program administrator. From the review, WPCTSA staff learned that current
participants had received mileage reimbursement benefits that did not fully align with past and/or
present service policies for trip purposes not defined as essential (e.g., church, visits with friends,
senior activity centers, etc.). Subsequent conversations with participants receiving these benefits
revealed that these trip purposes were still very important for a participant’s well-being despite
their exclusion from present policies. WPCTSA staff then re-examined how the current service
policies align with the Placer Rides Program’s overall mission/goal, which is to provide Placer
residents with a transportation assistance program that meets their needs when all other
transportation options are unavailable.

DISCUSSION
Attachment 1 identifies proposed changes that staff recommends for the Placer Rides Program’s
service policies to better align them with the Program’s mission/goal and the needs of Placer’s
residents. Significant proposed policy changes are summarized below:

    •   For “Rider (now defined as “Participant”) and Trip Eligibility”, a participant’s
        demographic qualifications (i.e., age, disability, and income) no longer define their
        eligibility and the proposed policies base eligibility on a participant’s unique
        transportation need that cannot be met with existing transit services and/or other
        transportation options available. Participants still must be residents of Placer County and
        unable to reasonably drive themselves to their destination.
    •   Additional trip purposes have been defined under “Essential Trips” to cover
        transportation needs that WPCTSA’s review highlighted were essential and undefined
        under current service policies.
    •   “Quality of Life Trips” has been added as a new category of allowable trip purposes for
        mileage reimbursement, defined as a destination visited for social, recreational,
        community, cultural, spiritual, or other life-enriching purposes. Up to five (5) of these

    •   Transportation to medical facilities outside of Placer County may now be eligible for

Committee (TAC) for the WPCTSA Board’s approval.

MEMORANDUM
TO:            PCTPA Board of Directors                                     DATE: October 28, 2026

FROM:          David Melko, Principal Transportation Planner

SUBJECT:       SR 65 PHASE 1 PROJECT CONSTRUCTION FUNDING AND
               AGREEMENT APPROVALS

ACTIONS REQUESTED
Adopt Resolution No. 26-38 as follows:
1. Conditionally approves entering into a Cooperative Agreement with Caltrans for construction of
   the SR 65 Phase 1 Project, with a not-to-exceed amount of $28,752,875, subject to SPRTA
   action on the local funding commitment.
2. Authorizes the Executive Director to execute the federal 2025 BUILD Grant Agreement for
   $22.48 million, designating Caltrans as the grant recipient and PCTPA as the subrecipient.
3. Recommends that the SPRTA Board approve the PCTPA allocation request in an amount not-
   to-exceed $10 million for construction and mitigation of the SR 65 Phase 1 Project.
4. Authorizes the Executive Director to negotiate the Construction Cooperative Agreement with
   Caltrans and authorizes the Chair and Executive Director to execute the Agreement.
5. Authorizes the Executive Director to negotiate and execute a mitigation credit purchase
   agreement with a U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service-approved conservation bank for the full SR 65
   Capacity and Operational Improvement Project, including Phase 1.

BACKGROUND
PCTPA, in cooperation with Caltrans, Placer County, and the Cities of Roseville, Rocklin, and
Lincoln, plans to widen approximately 6.3 miles of SR 65 in Placer County, from north of the
Galleria Boulevard/Stanford Ranch Road interchange to Lincoln Boulevard (post miles 6.5–12.8).
The project will address existing congestion, which occurs in both directions from approximately 7
a.m. to 7 p.m., and accommodate growing travel demand on SR 65, I-80, and the regional roadway
network. Improvements will enhance traffic operations, safety, and mobility while supporting
jurisdiction economic development goals.

The Project Report was approved on March 6, 2018. The CEQA Initial Study/Mitigated Negative
Declaration was adopted on December 11, 2017, and the NEPA Categorical Exclusion was signed
on March 27, 2018.

Implementation of the approved 6.3-mile project will be phased in accordance with the approved
planning documents and coordinated with delivery of the I-80/SR 65 Interchange Improvements
Project.

Phase 1 includes adding a third southbound lane between the Blue Oaks Boulevard and Galleria
Boulevard/Stanford Ranch Road interchanges, constructing an auxiliary lane from the Pleasant
Grove Boulevard on-ramp to the Galleria Boulevard off-ramp, and widening the Galleria Boulevard
off-ramp from one lane to two lanes.

DISCUSSION

SR 65 Phase 1 Advertisement Schedule
The project is scheduled for advertisement in December 2026, with construction anticipated to
begin in spring 2027. The schedule is tight: Caltrans requires an executed Construction Cooperative
Agreement to complete the Ready to List (RTL) process, and SPRTA’s funding commitment must
be secured before advertisement. To maintain the December schedule, the construction bid package
and all required agreements must be completed by the end of November.

If advertisement slips to January 2027 or later, the 100% design plans must be updated to comply
with the Manual for Assessing Safety Hardware (MASH). Caltrans has indicated that no
exemptions will be available beginning in 2027. Updating the final design plans, including Caltrans
review and approval, is expected to take at least six months, increasing design and construction
costs that PCTPA would ultimately need to cover with SPRTA funds.

Timely execution of the Construction Cooperative Agreement is therefore critical to maintaining the
project schedule and avoiding significant additional costs to PCTPA.

SR 65 Phase 1 Funding Plan
Phase 1 of the Project (PLA25529) is programmed for right-of-way acquisition and construction in
SACOG’s federally approved 2025–15 Metropolitan Transportation Improvement Program (MTIP).
Funding includes a $22.48 million federal BUILD grant awarded to PCTPA on July 15, 2025, and
$5.62 million in SPRTA funds for the local match, based on an estimated total project cost of $28.1
million.

Caltrans Department Furnished Materials (DFM) are unfortunately ineligible for federal funding,
DFM includes enhanced California Highway Patrol enforcement, traffic management plan, the
resident engineer’s office, and construction permits. Consequently, SPRTA’s local funding
commitment must increase by $652,875, from $5,620,000 to $6,272,875, to cover these costs.

Cooperative Agreement
The Construction Cooperative Agreement, including the funding and expenditure tables, is in final
draft form (Attachment 1) and under review by Caltrans Headquarters. Because the construction
cost estimate, including contingency, remains under review, construction costs in the funding table
have been increased by an additional five percent to provide the Executive Director flexibility in

PCTPA allocation request to SPRTA to cover potential mitigation costs for the full project,
including Phase 1, should compensation for the entire project be required before construction
advertisement. This amount is preliminary and should be considered a planning-level estimate.
Because mitigation credits cannot be purchased through the Placer County Conservation Program
(PCCP), staff will purchase the required credits from a U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service-approved
conservation bank.

BACKGROUND
The Placer–Sacramento Gateway Plan (PSGP) encompasses approximately 70 miles of Interstate 80,
State Route 65, and Business 80, serving a vital regional corridor that supports half of the Sacramento
region’s jobs and one-third of its residents, as well as freight, tourism, commuting, and economic
development.

The California Transportation Commission’s (CTC) 2025 Comprehensive Corridor Guidelines
recommend evaluating corridor plans in air quality nonattainment areas every four years. The original
PSGP, developed in 2019–2020, supported SB 1 funding nominations that secured nearly $133.4 million
in 2020 Solutions for Congested Corridors Program (SCCP) and Trade Corridor Enhancement Program
(TCEP) awards and $50 million in 2022 SCCP funding.

In July 2025, PCTPA received a Sustainable Transportation Competitive Planning Grant to fund the
update. In January 2026, the PCTPA Board approved a contract with Jacobs to prepare the PSGP
Update and authorized a Cooperative Agreement with the Sacramento Transportation Authority (STA)
to share the required local match.

The 2020 PSGP established a coordinated, regional investment strategy addressing corridor congestion,
improving safety and travel reliability, and strengthening multimodal mobility. The plan Update
reassessed project priorities, incorporated current transportation needs and conditions, and identified
competitive, implementation-ready improvements to position the region for future SB 1 funding
opportunities.

DISCUSSION

Placer-Sacramento Gateway Plan Update
A public review draft of the Placer–Sacramento Gateway Plan was released in September 2026. Staff
received one public favorable comment and acknowledged it in the final document, as appropriate. The
final Plan will be posted before the Board meeting at: https://www.pctpa.net/placer-sacramento-
gateway-plan-update. An Executive Summary is provided as Attachment 1. PCTPA staff and Jacobs
will present the final Plan, including projects proposed for the 2026 Solutions for Congested Corridors
Program (SCCP) Cycle 5 grant application.

The 10-month planning process culminated in an updated comprehensive multimodal corridor plan
addressing congestion, expanding travel choices, and improving environmental and quality-of-life
outcomes. The Plan identifies over 300 projects and 80 priority multimodal transportation projects
expected to be construction-ready by 2032, reinforcing regional collaboration. These priority projects
will improve corridor operations, expand travel options, and close gaps in the existing transportation
network.

To be eligible for SCCP funding, projects must be included in the Gateway Plan and demonstrate
benefits across key performance measures, including safety, congestion relief, accessibility, economic
development, job creation and retention, air quality, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, and efficient
land use. The California Transportation Commission (CTC) uses these measures to evaluate grant
applications. SCCP funds may support only non-capacity-increasing projects and the construction phase
of eligible improvements.

Projects for SCCP Cycle 5 Grant Application
The Gateway Plan prioritizes projects that effectively address corridor needs, are construction-ready,
and align with SCCP objectives. Four priority projects are recommended for inclusion in the SCCP
Cycle 5 grant application, due to the CTC in mid-November, and will be presented to the Board for
consideration.

Subsequent SCCP Grant Application Cycles
Implementation of the Gateway Plan will continue with preparation for future SCCP grant cycles, which
occur every two years, with the next cycle (Cycle 6) in 2028. Pre-Cycle 6 planning will prioritize
projects and advance their development and readiness to strengthen their competitiveness for SCCP
funding.

Staff Recommendation
Staff recommends that the Board accept the Placer–Sacramento Gateway Plan Update and authorize
submission of the SCCP Cycle 5 grant application to the CTC, in partnership with Caltrans, SACOG,
and STA, for projects identified in the Plan. The PCTPA TAC concurs with the staff recommendation.
